text:
Owen Power is finally producing like a first overall pick. He has 18 points in 24 games, 0.75 a game against 0.36 last season, and the Sabres have leaned on him for over 25 minutes a night, up from 21:39. Oddly, none of the points have come on the power play, a quirk Yahoo Sports pointed out even as he closes in on a career milestone.

The playmaking is real. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him at the 96th percentile among defensemen last season for primary shot assists, and at 5v5 Buffalo takes 52% of the expected goals with him on the ice, nearly five points better than without him. Evolving-Hockey also said he was better than his goals last year.

Two things to watch. The scoring rate (1.8 points per 60) is well above what we think he is (about 1.2), helped by shooting 10.7% on only 28 shots. And his minutes have slid to about 23 over his last ten games, three and a half fewer than his season average. If that trend holds, the breakout settles into something smaller but still better than before.
